headline: Large User Grid Cost Responsibility
short_summary: This bill mandates that large energy users, such as data centers, bear a greater share of the costs for new grid infrastructure and capacity, thereby reducing the financial burden on residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, Governor Abigail Spanberger's administration, environmental groups (e.g., Piedmont Environmental Council, Appalachian Voices), Dominion Energy (with amendments).
opponents: Data center industry (initially, due to increased costs), some business advocacy groups.
news_headline: Virginia requires data centers to pay for their own power lines
news_summary: Virginia's State Corporation Commission ruled that data centers must pay the full cost for the transmission infrastructure they require, preventing these costs from being shifted to residential ratepayers. This decision, supported by Governor Spanberger, is expected to save Virginia residents hundreds of millions of dollars.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates that water suppliers report the total volume of water provided to data centers, enhancing transparency and providing critical data for water resource management and planning.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups (e.g., Virginia League of Conservation Voters, Sierra Club), Senator Kannan Srinivasan, Delegate Elizabeth Guzman, Delegate Shelly Simonds, water conservation advocates, Virginia DEQ.
opponents: Data center industry (due to reporting burden or potential for future regulation), some business advocacy groups.
news_headline: Virginia Lawmakers Approve Legislation to Track Water Use by Data Centers
news_summary: The Virginia General Assembly passed SB 553, requiring water suppliers to report the total volume of water provided to data centers. This legislation aims to provide better data for policymakers and water resource planners to understand the industry's impact on Virginia's water resources, especially as data centers can use millions of gallons daily for cooling.

headline: Data Center Siting & Noise
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities, requiring site assessments for noise impacts on nearby residential units and schools, and allowing localities to consider other environmental impacts during siting.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local residents, community groups, environmental advocates (e.g., Virginia League of Conservation Voters), local governments, Delegate Joshua E. Thomas, Senator Danica A. Roem.
opponents: Data center industry, real estate developers, business advocacy groups (concerned about development restrictions).
news_headline: Spanberger pushes Virginia to rein in data center noise and pollution
news_summary: Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger has called for greater state regulation of data centers, citing concerns over noise levels and air pollution from backup generators impacting nearby communities. While HB 153 focuses on siting and noise assessments, broader state-level frameworks are being discussed to address these issues.
